---
guideline_id: ACC-2025-PCI-7.1
issuing_body: ACC
year: 2025
evidence_level: Class IIa
context_tags: [pci, access, calcification, CT]
---

Vascular access assessment before PCI. In patients with severe iliac or
femoral calcification planned for transfemoral percutaneous coronary
intervention, the recommendation is pre-procedural CT angiography of the
access route (Class IIa). Severe calcification of the iliofemoral segment on
CT substantially raises the risk of access failure and vascular
complications. The management recommendation is to image the entire access
route from the descending aorta to the common femoral artery, quantify
calcium burden and minimum luminal diameter, and select the access side with
the lesser burden. Alternative access (transradial, transaxillary, or
transsubclavian) should be considered when CT shows severe bilateral
calcification. This recommendation is reasonable and can be beneficial.
